instructions: Rinse the 1 1/2 cups rice in a few changes of cold water, swishing it with your hand, until the water runs mostly clear. Drain it well.

Put the rice in a small pot with 1 3/4 cups water and bring it to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to the lowest setting and cook for 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on for 10 minutes. A rice cooker works too.
Meanwhile, mince the 3 garlic cloves. In a small bowl, stir together the garlic, 1 tsp of the gochugaru, 1 tsp gochujang, 1 tbsp soy sauce and the 1/4 tsp pepper.
Cut 3 strips of bacon into 1 inch pieces. Put them in a wide shallow pot over medium and cook for about 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until the fat has run out and the edges are brown.

While the bacon cooks, slice half the Spam into pieces about 1/4 inch thick, 3 hot dogs on the diagonal and half the tofu into 1/2 inch slices. Thinly slice half the onion and all the mushrooms, and cut 3 scallions into 2 inch pieces. Cut 2 cups of the kimchi into bite size pieces.
Add the kimchi to the bacon and stir fry it for 2 to 3 minutes, until it softens and smells tangy.
Spread the onion around the kimchi. Arrange the Spam, hot dogs, tofu, mushrooms and scallions in piles on top, and spoon the seasoning into the middle.

Pour in the 4 cups broth and turn the heat up to medium high. Once it boils, stir the seasoning into the broth and turn the heat down to medium. Simmer for 8 to 10 minutes, until the onion is soft and the broth is deep orange.
Meanwhile, bring a small pot of water to a boil. Cook the ramen noodle block for 1 minute, until it loosens but is still firm, then drain it. Keep the flavor packet for another time.
Put the noodles in the middle of the stew and lay the 2 cheese slices on top. Simmer for 2 minutes, until the noodles are tender and the cheese has melted.
Taste the broth. If it's flat, add a splash more soy sauce.
Bring the pot to the table. Serve with the rice, and the last 2 tsp gochugaru in a small bowl on the side.
method_notes: Both read versions arrange kimchi, Spam, hot dogs, tofu, onion and mushrooms in a wide shallow pot, spoon a paste of gochugaru, gochujang, soy sauce and garlic on top, pour in stock and finish with instant ramen. Korean Bapsang uses bacon, anchovy or chicken broth and a lighter hand with the chili, and cooks the ramen separately first so it doesn't soak up the broth. Beyond Kimchee packs in more, with Vienna sausage, baked beans, minced pork, dumplings, rice cakes and a slice of cheese. This one follows Korean Bapsang, browns the bacon and kimchi in the pot first, adds the cheese, and puts most of the gochugaru on the side.
